questions.stem: 'This film was funny and exciting. I give it four stars.' Which type of text is this from?

explain.why: a notice gives plain information and does not rate anything
a forecast tells about the weather, not a film
a recipe tells the reader how to cook something

solution: The writer gives an opinion and a rating, as a review does.

questions.stem: 'Hi Sam, are you free on Saturday? Let's go cycling!' Which type of text is this from?

explain.why: a poem uses rhythm and images, but this invites a friend
a news report is about an event and is not addressed to one reader
instructions tell the reader how to do a task

solution: It speaks to one friend in a casual way and makes a plan.

questions.stem: 'First, put on your helmet. Next, sit on the seat. Finally, push the pedals.' Which type of text is this from?

explain.why: a story tells about characters and what happens to them
a news report tells what happened, but these lines tell what to do
a poem uses rhythm and images, but these lines give steps

solution: The steps are in order and tell the reader what to do.

questions.stem: Which word is often used to show the order of steps in instructions?

explain.why: 'Because' gives a reason, not order
'However' shows contrast, not order
'Although' shows contrast, not order

solution: 'Next' shows what step follows.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a typical opening of a story?
options: Buy one pair of shoes and get another free.
The Prime Minister spoke at the rally on Sunday.
One rainy afternoon, Mei found a strange key under her bed.
Add two cups of flour to the bowl.

explain.why: this is a line from an advertisement
this reports an event, as news does
this is a step from a recipe

solution: A time, a character and an interesting event start a story.

questions.stem: A poster says 'Keep Singapore clean.' What is the purpose of the poster?

explain.why: the words give a request and report nothing
the words are serious and tell people what to do
there is no character in the words

solution: The command reminds readers to do something.

questions.stem: Why does a story use words such as 'dark' and 'creepy'?
options: to ask the reader a string of questions
to list facts and figures about the place
to help the reader picture the scene
to give the reader steps to follow in order

explain.why: these words are not questions
these words describe, they do not give facts
a story does not give steps

solution: Describing words help readers see the setting in their mind.

questions.stem: A news report has the short headline 'Fire at Toa Payoh flat'. Why is it short?
options: to tell readers the main news quickly
to tell the whole story of the fire in detail
to give readers a recipe for a good dinner
to describe how the writer feels about fires

explain.why: a short line cannot hold the whole story
a headline has nothing to do with a recipe
a headline states the news, not feelings

solution: A short headline gives the main news at a glance.

questions.stem: Why does a notice use short, clear sentences?
options: so readers can enjoy a long story
so readers can guess the ending

explain.why: a notice gives information, not jokes
a notice is not a story
a notice has no ending to guess

solution: Short sentences are easy to read at a glance.

questions.stem: Which text is mostly written in the past tense?

explain.why: a recipe uses commands in the present
rules use commands and the present tense
a forecast uses the future tense

solution: A diary about yesterday tells what already happened.

questions.stem: Which text would you read to find out how to make a paper aeroplane?

explain.why: a news report tells what happened
a poem uses rhythm and images
a diary tells about someone's day

solution: Instructions tell the reader how to make or do something.

questions.stem: 'Dear Principal, I am writing to ask if we can have a longer recess.' Which type of letter does this begin?

explain.why: a story does not begin with 'Dear Principal'
a recipe does not begin like a letter
a poem is not written like a request to a principal

solution: It addresses a person in authority politely to make a request.

questions.stem: Which sign-off is suitable at the end of a letter to a close friend?

explain.why: 'The End' closes a story, not a letter
this ends an article or story, not a friendly letter
'Yours faithfully' is used in formal letters

solution: A friendly sign-off suits a letter to a close friend.

questions.stem: Which sentence states a fact?
options: Singapore is too hot for anyone.

explain.why: 'tastiest' is a personal opinion
'everyone loves' is an opinion that cannot be proved
'too hot' is an opinion that differs from person to person

solution: The year can be checked, so it is a fact.

questions.stem: Which sentence states an opinion?
options: Durians have a thick, spiky husk.
Durians are the most delicious fruit.
Durians are sold at many stalls in Geylang.
Durians grow on very tall trees in Johor.

explain.why: this can be checked by looking
this can be checked by visiting stalls
this can be checked by looking at the trees

solution: 'most delicious' depends on taste, so it is an opinion.

questions.stem: 'The wind howled angrily.' What does the word 'howled' do?
options: tells the reader to run away
gives the exact speed of the wind
makes the wind sound loud and wild
shows how to start a story

explain.why: 'howled' is not a command
'howled' gives a sound, not a number
a single word does not start a story

solution: 'howled' gives the wind a loud, wild sound.

questions.stem: In 'Mum said, "It is time for dinner!"', how does the writer show Mum's exact words?

explain.why: a heading is a title
brackets add extra information, not speech
bullet points make lists

solution: Speech marks go around the words a person says.

questions.stem: Which text usually has a title, a list of materials and numbered steps?

explain.why: a poem has lines and verses, not steps
a letter has a greeting and paragraphs, not numbered steps
a diary has a date and a personal account

solution: Craft instructions list what is needed and then give steps.

questions.stem: Which feature helps readers find information quickly in a school brochure?

explain.why: long paragraphs are slower to scan
speech marks show spoken words
rhyme does not help find facts

solution: Headings and bullet points let readers scan at a glance.

questions.stem: Why do news reports use reported speech such as 'The minister said that the park would open next year'?
options: to tell what someone said without quoting every word
to build suspense for the reader until the end
to make the whole report rhyme and sound nice
to give steps for the reader to follow

explain.why: a news report informs, not builds suspense
reported speech has nothing to do with rhyme
reported speech does not give steps

solution: Reported speech passes on what was said in the reporter's own words.

questions.stem: Which sentence from a review shows the writer's opinion?
options: The cast includes three well-known actors.
The film lasts about two hours in total.
I found the plot slow and predictable.
The film was released in cinemas in March.

explain.why: the number is a fact
the length is a fact
the date is a fact

solution: 'slow and predictable' is the writer's own judgement.

questions.stem: Which text is most likely to have headings such as 'Habitat' and 'Diet'?
options: a diary entry about a family trip
a story about a puppy that got lost
an information report about an animal

explain.why: a diary has dates, not topic headings
an advertisement is short and persuasive
a story is told in paragraphs without such headings

solution: Headings group facts about a topic in an information report.

questions.stem: An advertisement says, 'Imagine waking up to the smell of fresh bread.' What is the advertiser doing?
options: reporting a plain fact about how bread is made
giving steps for baking bread at home
inviting readers to picture a pleasant scene
telling readers a story about a young baker

explain.why: the line is not a statement of fact
there are no steps in the line
there is no character or plot

solution: The word 'Imagine' invites readers to picture something they would enjoy.

questions.stem: A speech opens with 'Good morning, principal, teachers and friends.' Why?
options: to report news about the school
to give the ending of the speech
to list steps for the audience

explain.why: it greets and does not report anything
this is how a speech starts, not ends
there are no steps here

solution: A speaker greets the listeners before the speech begins.

questions.stem: Why does a story often use the past tense?
options: it tells events that have already happened
it states facts that are always true everywhere
it gives the reader instructions to follow
it makes predictions about what happens tomorrow

explain.why: that is the job of the present tense
stories do not instruct
that would use the future tense

solution: The narrator tells what happened in the story.

questions.stem: Why does a writer of instructions use words such as 'carefully' and 'gently'?
options: to show how to do a step
to tell the reader a secret

explain.why: instructions are meant to be clear
these words do not tell a secret
these words are not chosen for rhyme

solution: These adverbs tell the reader the way to do the action.

questions.stem: Why do advertisements use words such as 'new', 'free' and 'best'?
options: to make readers want the product
to give the history of the product

explain.why: these words sound happy and sell
these words say nothing about history
these words do not teach

solution: These words make the product sound attractive.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the topic sentence of a paragraph about recycling?
options: Blue bins are placed near the lifts.
Paper is collected every Tuesday morning.
Recycling helps to protect our environment.
Many pupils bring bottles from home.

explain.why: this is a detail that supports the topic
this is a detail that supports the topic
this is a detail that supports the topic

solution: The topic sentence states the main idea that the details support.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the best ending for a letter asking the school to build a bicycle rack?
options: Many pupils like cycling in the park.
I hope you will consider my request.

explain.why: this is not related to the request
this adds a new fact instead of closing
this does not close the letter or the request

solution: A polite closing line repeats the request.

questions.stem: Which set of words helps to order events in a recount?

explain.why: these words give examples
these words show contrast or condition
these words show reasons or results

solution: 'first, then, finally' show the order in which things happened.

questions.stem: Which tense is mostly used in a recount of a school trip?

explain.why: a recount does not give commands
the trip has already happened
the trip is not happening now

solution: A recount tells what happened, so it uses the past tense.

questions.stem: Why do writers use 'I' in a diary?
options: because they are giving orders to other people
because they are reporting the news to readers
because they write about their own experience
because they are describing a total stranger

explain.why: 'I' is not used to give orders
a news report uses the third person
'I' is the writer, not a stranger

solution: A diary tells the writer's own thoughts and events.

questions.stem: Which sentence in a persuasive text gives a reason?
options: Plastic bags harm sea animals, so we should use them less.
Bags come in many different colours and sizes.
Plastic bags are sold at most supermarkets.
I bought a plastic bag at the shop yesterday.

explain.why: this describes bags but gives no reason
this states a fact but gives no reason
this tells what the writer did

solution: 'harm sea animals' is the reason for using fewer bags.

questions.stem: A writer says the character 'whispered' instead of 'shouted'. What does 'whispered' show?
options: that the character was far away
that the character was telling a lie
that the character spoke very softly

explain.why: 'whispered' says nothing about distance
'whispered' says nothing about lying
'shouted' means loudly, not 'whispered'

solution: 'whispered' means to speak in a very quiet voice.

questions.stem: 'Her eyes were as bright as stars.' What kind of language is this?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not tell anyone to do something
eyes are not really the same as stars

solution: A simile compares two things using 'as' or 'like'.

questions.stem: 'The classroom was a zoo.' What kind of language is this?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not tell anyone to do something
a simile uses 'as' or 'like', which are not here

solution: A metaphor says one thing is another, without 'as' or 'like'.

questions.stem: In 'The balloon burst with a loud bang.', which word imitates a sound?

explain.why: 'burst' names an action
'loud' describes the sound
'balloon' names a thing

solution: 'bang' sounds like the noise it names.

questions.stem: Why does the writer use a colon in 'You will need: flour, sugar and eggs'?

explain.why: ownership uses an apostrophe
spoken words use speech marks
a question uses a question mark

solution: A colon introduces a list that follows.

questions.stem: A weather report says, 'Showers are expected in the afternoon.' Why does it use 'expected'?
options: because a forecast cannot be certain
because the writer is telling a story
because the showers have already stopped

explain.why: 'expected' is not a command
a forecast is not a story
'expected' looks ahead, not back

solution: A forecast says what is likely, not what is sure.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written in a formal tone?
options: I would be grateful if you could reply by Friday
Get back to me soon, please
Tell me whenever you feel like it

explain.why: this is friendlier but less formal
this is casual and vague
this is casual and blunt

solution: Polite, full wording is formal.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written in an informal tone?
options: I am writing to inform you of a change
We regret to announce the closure

explain.why: this is formal
this is formal
this is formal

solution: Casual greetings and questions are informal.

questions.stem: Why does a persuasive writer say 'We must protect our reefs'?
options: to include readers and make them feel part of the cause
to give the exact number of reefs in the sea
to tell the story of one special reef
to ask readers a question about reefs

explain.why: there is no number in the sentence
the sentence tells no story
the sentence is not a question

solution: 'We' and 'our' bring the reader in as a team member.

questions.stem: An essay writer says, 'Many experts agree that exercise is important.' What is the purpose of these words?
options: to describe what the experts look like
to ask the reader a difficult question
to make the argument stronger by showing support
to tell a story about a group of experts

explain.why: no appearance is described
the sentence is not a question
the sentence tells no story

solution: Naming agreement from experts supports the writer's claim.

questions.stem: Why does an information report use the present tense, as in 'Otters live near rivers'?
options: because it makes plans for the near future
because it tells a story from a long time ago
because it states general facts that are true now
because it gives orders to its readers

explain.why: the sentence is not about the future
a report states facts, not a story
the sentence is not a command

solution: General facts that stay true are written in the present tense.

questions.stem: Why might a writer use short sentences during a chase scene?
options: to give a long list of facts
to slow down the action of the scene
to speed up the pace and build tension
to explain a science idea to readers

explain.why: a chase scene is not a list
short sentences make a scene feel faster
a chase scene tells action

solution: Short sentences feel quick and urgent.

questions.stem: A story ends with 'She never saw the old house again.' What does this sentence do?
options: brings the story to a close

explain.why: a story does not give steps
the sentence is not a question
an introduction comes at the start

solution: It tells what happened last, so the story ends.

questions.stem: A speaker repeats, 'Never give up! Never give up!' What is the effect?
options: it stresses the message so the audience remembers it
it makes the speech sound rather uncertain
it tells the audience a short story
it gives many new facts to the audience

explain.why: repetition makes it sound firm
there is no story in the words
repeating adds no new facts

solution: Repeating a phrase helps listeners remember it.

questions.stem: Which phrase is an exaggeration typical of advertisements?
options: noodles sold for only two dollars a bowl
noodles made with wheat flour and water
the tastiest noodles in the whole universe
noodles served hot with a bowl of soup

explain.why: this is a plain fact
this is a plain fact
this is a plain fact

solution: 'in the whole universe' is too big to be true, so it is an exaggeration.

questions.stem: Why do news reports often begin with the most important facts?
options: so readers get the main point at once
so the ending is a surprise
so readers do not need the headline

explain.why: news reports do not aim for a surprise ending
rhyme has nothing to do with it
the headline still has a job

solution: Busy readers see the key facts first.

questions.stem: A letter begins 'Dear Sir or Madam'. Which ending is correct?

explain.why: 'Love from' is for family and close friends
'Yours sincerely' is for a named person
'See you soon' is casual

solution: If you do not know the name, close with 'Yours faithfully'.

questions.stem: A letter begins 'Dear Mr Tan'. Which ending is correct?

explain.why: 'Yours faithfully' is for an unnamed reader
'Love from' is for family and close friends
'See you soon' is casual

solution: If you know the name, close with 'Yours sincerely'.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a recommendation in a book review?
options: The book was published in Singapore last year.
The book has about 250 pages in all.
I would recommend this book to anyone who enjoys mysteries.
The author of the book lives in Singapore.

explain.why: this is a fact about its date
this is a fact about length
this is a fact about the author

solution: The writer advises who should read the book.

questions.stem: Why might a writer begin a story with dialogue?
options: to list the main facts of the story first
to explain to readers how to do something
to give readers a short news report
to draw the reader straight into the action

explain.why: dialogue is spoken words, not a list
dialogue does not give steps
dialogue is not news

solution: Spoken words put the reader in the middle of a scene.

questions.stem: A diary about a family trip is written mostly in which person?

explain.why: the writer would say 'he' or 'she' about others only
a diary mainly says 'I' and 'we'
'you' is rare in a diary

solution: The writer tells 'I' and 'we' experiences.

questions.stem: What makes 'Wake up! Step up! Speak up!' memorable?
options: a repeated pattern of short commands
the past tense of each verb

explain.why: the words are short, not long
there are no facts or figures
the verbs are commands, not past tense

solution: Repeating a pattern makes words easy to remember.

questions.stem: Why does a museum brochure include opening hours and ticket prices?
options: to tell a story about how the museum began
to describe how the objects look inside
to give practical information visitors need
to make the whole brochure rhyme nicely

explain.why: these details are not a story
these details are not about objects
these details are not for rhyme

solution: Visitors need these facts to plan a visit.

questions.stem: Which sentence shows the writer's stance clearly in a persuasive essay on homework?
options: Once upon a time, a boy hated his homework.
Yesterday I finished my homework at nine o'clock.
Homework is work that teachers give to pupils.
Homework takes up too much of our time, and it is time for a change.

explain.why: this starts a story
this recounts what the writer did
this defines the word and takes no stance

solution: It says clearly what the writer wants.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a statistic to support an argument?
options: Some of our pupils feel very tired.
Pupils sometimes feel tired in the afternoon.
Nine out of ten pupils in our school said they felt tired after a long day.
Many of the pupils feel tired after school.

explain.why: 'some' gives no number
'sometimes' gives no number
'many' gives no number

solution: 'Nine out of ten' is a number that backs up the claim.

questions.stem: Why does a news report put a quotation in speech marks?
options: to show the title of the whole report
to show a list of items in the report
to show these are the speaker's exact words
to show that the words are meant as a joke

explain.why: a title does not need speech marks
a list is not shown with speech marks
speech marks do not mean a joke

solution: Speech marks show the exact words someone said.
